content: FOXA1, also referred to as Forkhead box protein A1 or hepatocyte nuclear factor 3-alpha (HNF-3A), is a protein encoded by the FOXA1 gene in humans. FOXA1 belongs to the forkhead class of DNA-binding proteins. These proteins, known as hepatocyte nuclear factors, function as transcriptional activators for liver-specific genes, such as albumin and transthyretin. Additionally, FOXA1 interacts with chromatin as a pioneer factor, facilitating chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. In mice, similar family members are involved in metabolic regulation and play critical roles in the differentiation of the pancreas and liver. In the context of breast cancer, FOXA1 expression is strongly associated with the presence of ERα+ (estrogen receptor alpha-positive), GATA3+, and PR+ (progesterone receptor-positive) protein expression, as well as endocrine signaling pathways. FOXA1 acts as a pioneer factor for ERα in ERα+ breast cancers, and its expression may identify cancers that undergo rapid reprogramming of ERα signaling. This reprogramming is linked to poor clinical outcomes and resistance to treatment. Conversely, in ERα− (estrogen receptor alpha-negative) breast cancers, FOXA1 expression is associated with low-grade tumor morphology and improved disease-free survival. FOXA1 is a downstream target of GATA3 in the mammary gland. In ERα− cancers, FOXA1 expression may help identify a subset of tumors that respond to alternative endocrine therapies, such as treatments targeting androgen receptor antagonists. In prostate cancer, mutations in the FOXA1 gene have been recurrently observed, suggesting a significant role in the pathogenesis of this malignancy.
